items.title: Laurence Juber interviewed by Monk Rowe, Glasgow, Scotland, July 27, 2016 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: on the plane I watched “Miles Ahead,” the Don Cheadle movie that’s like the biopic about Miles

ctx.x: Yeah. So you learn how to be accurate. But the ultimate thing I think is having that kind of faith that it will work out. Because it can be kind of scary sometimes. And orchestrators don’t always know how to write for guitar. Often you’ll see a chord that you know is unplayable, and you’re sight reading and it’s like okay what’s going to work in this context. And I’ve seen guitar players come across a — because they’ll see a G 7 chord in the jazz context, but they won’t play the right voicing. They’ll play like a…
major chord is always a C major chord. It doesn’t matter what style. You just have to know how to voice it.
